# 2 Baruch Chapter 45 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 45 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 45:1 — "think / meditate"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Think-therefore upon-these-things" | Literal: Syriac ethar = think/reflect |
| LOGOS | "Meditate therefore on these things" | "Meditate" adds depth of engagement |
| PNEUMA | "take all of this to heart" | Paraphrase emphasizing internalization |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "Meditate." The Syriac term suggests sustained reflection, and "meditate" captures this better than the bare "think."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 45:4 — "light of beauty / blazing light of beauty / beautiful light"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "light-[of-beauty]" | Brackets "of beauty" as possible gloss |
| LOGOS | "the light of beauty" | Full phrase without bracket |
| PNEUMA | "a blazing light of beauty" | Adds "blazing" for visual impact |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the light of beauty." The Syriac nuhra d-shapira = light of beauty/splendor. "Blazing" (PNEUMA) adds an element not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 45:4 — "made like the stars / shine like the stars"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they-will-be-made-[like]-the-stars" | Brackets "like" as implied |
| LOGOS | "they will be made like the stars" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "they will shine like the stars" | Interpretive — adds the shining quality |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained LOGOS "they will be made like the stars." The Syriac says "made/become like" — the transformation is the point, not specifically the shining. PNEUMA's addition of "shine" is an interpretation of how they are like stars (cf. Dan 12:3) but is not explicit in 2 Baruch's text here.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Syriac preserved without interpretive addition.

---

## 45:5 — "will not be able to resist / unable to resist it"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "will-not-be-able-to-resist" | Literal: cannot withstand/stand against |
| LOGOS | "will not be able to resist it" | Adds "it" as object |
| PNEUMA | "find themselves unable to resist it" | Adds "find themselves" for natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "will not be able to resist it." Clean and clear. PNEUMA's "find themselves" adds unnecessary verbiage.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
